title: H3 Grid Support
text: H3 hierarchical hexagonal grid system developed Uber. partitions Earth’s surface hexagonal cells 16 resolutions (0–15), roughly 7×\times finer last. Cell IDs 64-bit integers encoded hexadecimal strings (e.g., "8528342bfffffff"). H3 widely adopted: FCC uses broadband mapping, Foursquare POI analytics, DuckDB/BigQuery native H3 extensions. Key difference ISEA: H3 cells equal-area. Cell area varies ~1.6×\times largest smallest hexagons given resolution, depending latitude. rigorous equal-area analysis, use ISEA. interoperability H3 ecosystems, use type = "h3".

what: The Problem: Equal-Area Grids on a Sphere
title: Mathematical Foundations
text: projection sphere plane must distort something. spatial statistics, need cells equal area regardless location. Standard latitude-longitude grids fail badly: 1° cell equator covers ~12,300 km², cell near poles covers tiny fraction . ISEA projection solves : Inscribing regular icosahedron sphere Projecting spherical “cap” onto corresponding flat triangular face using modified Lambert equal-area projection Overlaying hexagonal grid resulting planar triangles

title: Mathematical Foundations
text: foundation Snyder’s projection Lambert’s azimuthal equal-area projection, developed Johann Heinrich Lambert 1772. projection maps sphere radius RR tangent plane preserving area exactly (Snyder, 1987, p. 182).

title: Mathematical Foundations

text: Spatial binning fundamental ecological modeling, epidemiology, geographic analysis. Standard approaches using rectangular lat-lon grids introduce severe area distortions: 1° cell equator covers ~12,300 km², cell near poles covers fraction area. violates equal-sampling assumption underlying spatial statistics. Discrete Global Grid Systems (DGGS) solve partitioning Earth’s surface cells uniform area. hexify’s primary backend ISEA (Icosahedral Snyder Equal Area): true equal-area hexagonal grids apertures 3, 4, 7, mixed 4/3, implemented C++ external dependencies. interoperability industry ecosystems (FCC, Foursquare, DuckDB), hexify also supports H3 grids via vendored C library.
